headline: Continued a $1.00 rent abatement in Harris v Parmar and two Seramonte LLC cases; directed a landlord to stop retaliatory action.
summary: Heard the Concepcion v McKeon case; the motion calls for no retaliation and compliance with health district repairs. Continued three matters, dismissed two cases, and closed the Taylor v Rodriguez case.
decisions: Approved the July 16, 2026 special meeting minutes.
Approved the August 6, 2026 regular meeting minutes.
Continued the Vincent v Seramonte LLC case (FRC-260723-J).
Dismissed the Outlaw v Napoleon case (FRC-260802-G).
Continued the Jean-Francois v Seramonte LLC case (FRC-260807-G).
Motion to order the landlord to stop retaliatory action and comply with health district repairs; follow-up at the October meeting. The minutes give no vote count.
Dismissed the Gomez v Pinguil case (FRC-260807-G).
Continued rent abatement at $1.00 until the apartment meets housing codes; revisit at the next meeting.
Closed the Taylor v Rodriguez case after the health district reported it closed on August 10, 2026.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Fair Rent Commission Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
6:00 PM, September 3, 2026 
  
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
fairrent@Hamden.com 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER   
 
 
  1. Commissioner Roll Call  
  Chair Commissioner Cunningham called the meeting to order at 6:03 P.M. 
Commissioner Vice Chair Conte Robinson present 
Commissioner Amy Molina present 
Commissioner Chanelle Goldson present 
Commissioner Greta Johnson present 
Quorum established 
Attorney Tim Lee present 
Director Karen Bivens present 
Commissioner Jennifer Paradis absent 
Commissioner Jacob Marrandino absent 
Commissioner Antwan Nedd absent 
2. ATTENDANCE   
 
 
  1. FRC-260810-F Concepcion V McKeon  
  
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES   
 
 
  1. Fair Rent Commission Special Meeting July 16, 2026 Minutes.pdf  
  Motion Passed. 
  2. Fair Rent Commission Regular Meeting August 6, 2026_Minutes_Preview.pdf  
  Motion Passed. 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT   
 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE
1. FRC-260723-J Vincent v Seramonte LLC — Continuance requested. 
FRC-260802-G Outlaw V Napoleon - Tenant was served a Notice to Quit for 
nonpayment of rent. 
FRC-260807-G Jean-Francois V Seramonte LLC- Continuance requested. 
FRC-260807-G-Gomez v Pinguil — Tenant and Landlord reached an agreement to 
keep the rent at its current rate.  
  
 
6. CASES TO BE HEARD   
 
 
 1. FRC-260723-J Vincent v Seramonte LLC 
       
  Motion: Continuance was requested. Motioned by Commission Chair Cunningham, 
2nd Commissioner Johnson. 
 2. FRC-260802-G Outlaw V Napoleon 
       
  Motion: Case dismissed. Motioned by Commission Chair Cunningham, 2nd 
Commissioner Robinson. 
 3. FRC-260807-G Jean-Francois V Seramonte LLC 
       
  Motion: Continuance was requested.Motioned by Commission Chair Cunningham, 
2nd Commissioner Johnson. 
 4. FRC-260810-F Concepcion V McKeon 
       
  Candice Concepcion, tenant, was sworn in by Commission Chair Cunningham and 
gave testimony. Geraldine McKeon, landlord, was sworn in by Commission Chair 
Cunningham and gave testimony.  
Motion: Cease and desist from any retaliatory action on the part of the landlord 
pursuant to the Connecticut General Statutes and applicable Fair Rent Commission 
ordinances. Continue to fully comply with any repairs or remediation ordered by 
Quinnipiack Valley Health District (QVHD) on August 13, 2026. The Commission will 
request a copy of the QVHD report when it becomes available and will follow up with 
the parties regarding the status of the matter at the October meeting. Motioned by 
Chair Peter Cunningham, 2nd Commissioner Molina. 
 5. FRC-260807-G-Gomez v Pinguil 
       
  Motion: Case dismissed. Motioned by Commission Chair Cunningham, 2nd 
Commissioner Molina. 
7. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 No Executive Sessions 
8. REPORTS   
 
 
9. OLD BUSINESS   
 
 
  1. FRC-260421-K Harris V Parmar
Motion: Continue rent abatement at $1.00 pursuant to the Commission’s previous 
orders until the apartment is brought into compliance with applicable housing codes. 
The Commission will revisit the matter at its next meeting. Motioned by Commission 
Chair Cunningham, 2nd Commissioner Robinson. 
  2. FRC-260313-H Taylor V Rodriguez  
  Motion: Quinnipiack Valley Health District reported their case closed on August 10, 
2026. Case closed. Motioned by Commission Chair Cunningham, 2nd Commissioner 
Molina. 
10. NEW BUSINESS   
 No New Business 
11. ADJOURNMENT   
 The meeting was adjourned at 7:23 p.m.
